sentences.text: The genus Libonectes was established by Carpenter in 1997, reclassifying a species originally described as Elasmosaurus morgani by Welles in 1949.

The name Libonectes means 'southern swimmer' because many specimens were found in southern North America, while the species name 'morgani' honors Charles Gill Morgan, who acquired the first fossils found by T.W. Tidwell in the late 1930s.
The complete specimen of Libonectes measured 7.2 meters in length, and the type specimen had a neck measuring 5.06 meters long.

Libonectes had taller neural spines and longer supporting processes on its neck vertebrae compared to Thalassomedon, and the type specimen of L. morgani contains the best-preserved elasmosaurid skull known.
The type specimen possessed a neck measuring 5.06 meters long.
The type specimen of L. morgani contains the best-preserved elasmosaurid skull known.
While its teeth suggest a carnivorous diet, gastroliths found in fossils suggest Libonectes may have been omnivorous.
Libonectes likely hunted in deep waters for small fish and ammonites due to its large size preventing it from entering shallow waters.
Researchers suspect Libonectes used its large size to trap prey because it was a slow swimmer.

Libonectes fossils are found in the Britton Formation of Texas and the Akrabou Formation of Morocco from the lower Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, and the animal lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
